name: Dölsach
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Drautal Valley, featuring the Aguntum Roman ruins and a castle.
beschreibung:
Overview

Dölsach is a sun-drenched and historically rich municipality in East Tyrol within the Lienz district, situated at an altitude of approximately 678 meters in the fertile Lienz basin. Home to roughly 2,330 residents, the town lies five kilometers east of the district capital Lienz, spanning the broad Drau Valley floor up to the slopes of the Iselsberg pass and Mount Ederplan (2,062 m). Famed as the site of Tyrol's sole ancient Roman city, Dölsach enjoys a mild basin climate, centuries-old fruit orchard heritage, and dramatic panoramic vistas of the craggy Lienzer Dolomites, including Mount Spitzkofel and the Laserzwand. Its historic hamlets such as Dölsach, Stribach, and Gödnach lend the community vibrant rural charm.

History

Dölsach occupies a unique place in alpine archaeology: around 50 AD, Roman Emperor Claudius granted municipal charter to Municipium Claudium Aguntum, making it the only ancient Roman city in present-day Tyrol. As a prosperous trade and administrative center in the province of Noricum at the nexus of major transalpine routes, Aguntum flourished with opulent public baths, a civic market (macellum), and atrium villas, until it was destroyed in the 7th century following Slavic conflicts and catastrophic floods. Dölsach was first recorded in writing on August 19, 1197; its name derives from the Slavic dolice, meaning little valley. The parish church of Saint Martin traces its roots back to a 10th-century Romanesque church; rebuilt after a disastrous village fire in 1853, it features a prized high altarpiece painted in 1872 by celebrated Tyrolean master Franz von Defregger. Furthermore, the world-renowned Austrian painter Albin Egger-Lienz was born in the hamlet of Stribach in 1868.

How to Get There

By car, Dölsach is reached via the Drautal federal highway B100 in just five minutes from Lienz; from Carinthia access leads via Spittal an der Drau, and from Salzburg via the Großglockner highway B107 crossing the Iselsberg pass. Rail travelers use the Drau Valley Railway: Dölsach station is served hourly by Tyrolean S-Bahn trains (line S1) and regional trains between Lienz and Spittal-Millstätter See. Regular regional buses link the village directly to Lienz.

Tips

The top attraction is the Archaeological Park and Museum of Aguntum, where visitors can explore excavated Roman thermal baths, villas, and markets, taking in panoramas from an 18-meter-high observation tower set against the Dolomites. Dölsach is celebrated as East Tyrol's premier distilling village, boasting over forty active distilleries; the Kuenzhof estate in Gödnach treats guests to a 400-year distilling heritage, guided tastings of genuine Osttiroler Pregler fruit brandy, and award-winning single malt whisky. Hikers can summit Mount Ederplan to relax at the Anna-Schutzhaus lodge, while cyclists cruise along the famous Drau Cycle Path R1 through the valley floor.
